state.context:
Identify which syntax idea, if any, merits the next targeted review for canlang. It is an AI-authored DSL for CRUD-centered company SaaS, with adoption as the leading goal and token economy, dependable generation and low complexity supporting it. Today it uses single-space nesting, one package Given/When/Then skeleton, typed scenario/do execution, explicit access decisions, checked atomic set writes and embedded independently written behavior examples. Executable tools and empirical token/generation evaluations are absent. Field punning such as {name}, reusable Model.field validation/types, pure helper derivations and declarative SQL-shaped query clauses already exist and are not additions.
Official documentation offers five candidate ideas. Refinements draws on CUE constrained reusable definitions, illustrated as type ShortText = text trim min=1 max=120 for multiple fields. Shared validation could avoid copying bounds, but existing field-type reuse may suffice; new aliases could conceal differences in business validation, and structural/nominal identity needs definition. Enum_match borrows Rust exhaustive state branching: every member of a closed enum gets an arm, with action effects remaining inside do. It could surface omitted states and shorten chains of repeated comparisons, yet expands branching grammar and can force empty/unhelpful cases.
Compound_updates borrows the Python += spelling only inside canonical set, e.g. set counter {value+=1}. It could avoid repeating the record/field for additions and subtraction; a narrow corpus scan identified seven simple same-variable cases and did not cover nested-record paths. Simultaneous field evaluation, checked overflow, money, locks and versions still require defined behavior; Python's overloadable in-place mutations and bare storage assignment would not be inherited. Null_ops adapts Kotlin ?. plus ECMAScript ?? for pure reads and fallback. Shorter nullable expressions are possible, but precedence, nullable propagation and short-circuit behavior must be specified; null handling never grants private access.
Required_scalars follows Kotlin non-null defaults: bare stored scalar types would mean required inputs, while nullable ?, creation defaults, server values and current array defaults/exceptions retain their meanings. Bare required operation parameters already use this convention; current stored scalars instead need ! without a default/server expression. The earlier audit found 798 scalar markers and 18 required-array exceptions. This candidate can reduce common repeated suffixes but needs a complete declaration/spec migration without altering array input requirements. None of these sketches is adopted syntax, and no borrowed object system, arbitrary macros or general runtime is proposed.
Select a first investigation rather than an approved implementation. Weigh expected occurrence benefits against parsing/semantic costs without equating source brevity to measured model-token gains. Leave the decision open if comparative evidence is inadequate.

review_priority.instructions: Select the most worthwhile first investigation, balancing likely reuse against additional grammar and semantic commitments.

criteria.refinements: Examine shared scalar validation definitions for repeated field constraints.
criteria.enum_match: Examine a closed-enum match form that requires all states to be covered.
criteria.defer: Postpone new syntax because the supplied comparisons do not establish a priority.
criteria.compound_updates: Examine += and -= field updates only as part of canonical set.
criteria.null_ops: Examine nullable-member access plus compact null fallback in read expressions.
criteria.required_scalars: Examine dropping scalar ! through non-null required field defaults, retaining other field modes.
